SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.    File No............
S.5, Special Branch Station, 256
REPORT
Date October 6, 1939. 0 39
Subject (in full) S.M.C. and Labour Disputes.
Made by ............ and ............ Forwarded by D.S. Pharazyn

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE / OCT 7 1939 / DEPT. SPECIAL BRANCH）

With reference to the attached translation
of a report entitled "S.M.C. to devise ways and means
to remove disputes between capital and labour" from the
"Central China Daily News" (中華日報), a propaganda
organ of Wang Ching-wei, of October 1, enquiries made
by this Section show that the article in question is a
translation made from the "Shanghai Mainichi," a local
Japanese language daily, of September 26, a cutting
from which is attached.

D. S. Pharazyn
D. S.

D. C. (Special Branch)

The "Central China Daily News" published the following
report on October 1, 1939 :-

S.M.C. TO DEVISE WAYS AND MEANS TO REMOVE DISPUTES
BETWEEN CAPITAL AND LABOUR

Owing to the daily increasing cost of living
in Shanghai, the labour class, whose wages are small,
are finding it difficult to maintain their livelihood,
therefore, they have requested their employers to grant
them an increase of pay. Disputes between Capital and
Labour have been of frequent occurrence in the Foreign
Settlements during the past several months, especially
in August and September when scores of labour disputes
took place.

According to information secured from the S.M.C.,
in view of the fact that lack of mediators had often
caused a dispute to reach a deadlock, Major Bourne,
Commissioner of Police, will undertake mediation work
together with capitalists, while the Shanghai Capital and
Labour Investigation Association will be the principal
body to undertake such mediations. Two days ago,
managements of large local factories met in a certain
hotel on Avenue Joffre, at which many matters such as
increase of wages for workers in view of the increasing
cost of living were discussed.

In future workers intending to submit demands
to their managements should first discuss the matter with
the Capital and Labour Investigation Association and the
Association will then mediate and satisfy both parties.
In this way, no more labour disputes will occur in the
Settlements.

CWC

REPORT
Date. September 29, 39.

Subject. The Capital and Labour Investigation Association - article
published in the Mainichi of September 26, 1939.
Made by. C.D.I. Sih Tse Liang    Forwarded by. R. W. Mac Aulie D. I.

（批：O.P.S. Musgrove made inquiries at French and all I got from him was that the article is the outcome of something himself told a reporter. Thos Robertson D.C. 513）

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 2 OCT. 1939 M3）

The report published in the Mainichi of September
26, 1939, to the effect that "The Shanghai Capital and
Labour Investigation Association , an arbitration body
to act between capital and labour, through the good
offices of Major Bourne, Commissioner of Police, called
a meeting at a restaurant on Avenue Joffre on September
20 to solve matters concerning disputes between capital
and labour," cannot be confirmed.

The existence of the so-called "Capital and
Labour Investigation Association" is unknown to any
of the following organizations which have been approached
by the Special Branch :-

Industrial Section, S.M.C.,
China Office of the International Labour Bureau,
Chinese Chamber of Commerce,
Shanghai Citizens' Federation,
Chinese Ratepayers' Association.

The French Police have also no knowledge of the
meeting alleged to have been held in the French
Concession on September 20, 1939.

Sih Tse Liang
C. D. I.

D. C.(Special Branch).

September 26, 1939.

MAINICHI

THE CAPITAL AND LABOUR INVESTIGATION ASSOCIATION
TO ARBITRATE DISPUTES BETWEEN CAPITAL
AND LABOUR

The recent fall in the value of
the legal tender note coupled with the high price of
commodities is responsible for the frequent disputes
between capital and labour in the Foreign Settlements.
The Shanghai Capital and Labour
Investigation Association, an arbitration body to act
between capital and labour, through the good offices
of Major Bourne, Commissioner of the S.M.P., called a
meeting of a large number of persons concerned at a
restaurant on Avenue Joffre on September 20 to solve
matters concerning disputes between capital and labour.
The number of disputes between
capital and labour which took place in August and
September in the Settlement is reported to have been
more than 20, the majority of which was caused by the
increased price of commodities resulting in the demand
for increases of pay. The Settlement authorities
have been considering a plan to deal with the matter;
however, the Shanghai Capital and Labour Investigation
Association, being requested by capitalists who fear
that labour trouble may affect their enterprises has
commenced activities to deal with the matter.
As a result of the meeting held
with the persons concerned, the Shanghai Capital and
Labour Investigation Association has informed the
labourers of all factories and mills connected with the
Association to inform that body of any causes for
dissatisfaction before drafting demands. This timely
movement of the Association is reported to have been
greatly appreciated by all quarters concerned.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 27 SEPT. 1939）

September 26, 1939.

MAINICHI

THE CAPITAL AND LABOUR INVESTIGATION ASSOCIATION
TO ARBITRATE DISPUTES BETWEEN CAPITAL
AND LABOUR

The recent fall in the value of
the legal tender note coupled with the high price of
commodities is responsible for the frequent disputes
between capital and labour in the Foreign Settlements.
The Shanghai Capital and Labour
Investigation Association, an arbitration body to act
between capital and labour, through the good offices
of Major Bourne, Commissioner of the S.M.P., called a
meeting of a large number of persons concerned at a
restaurant on Avenue Joffre on September 20 to solve
matters concerning disputes between capital and labour.
The number of disputes between
capital and labour which took place in August and
September in the Settlement is reported to have been
more than 20, the majority of which was caused by the
increased price of commodities resulting in the demand
for increases of pay. The Settlement authorities
have been considering a plan to deal with the matter,
however, the Shanghai Capital and Labour Investigation
Association, being requested by capitalists who fear
that labour trouble may affect their enterprises has
commenced activities to deal with the matter.
As a result of the meeting held
with the persons concerned, the Shanghai Capital and
Labour Investigation Association has informed the
labourers of all factories and mills connected with the
Association to inform that body of any causes for
dissatisfaction before drafting demands. This timely
movement of the Association is reported to have been
greatly appreciated by all quarters concerned.
